redFlags.title: Common Scam Red Flags
redFlags.intro: Scammers often use the same tricks. Learn to recognize these common red flags to protect yourself.

flags.title: Sense of Urgency
flags.description: Scammers try to create panic to make you act without thinking. They might say your grant will be cancelled if you don't act immediately.

flags.title: Request for Payment
flags.description: SASSA will never ask you to pay a fee to receive a grant. If someone asks you for money, it's a scam.

flags.title: Requests for Personal Information
flags.description: Be very careful about sharing your ID number, banking details, or PIN. SASSA will never ask for your bank card PIN.

flags.title: Suspicious Links
flags.description: Do not click on links in SMS or email messages that claim to be from SASSA. These links can lead to fake websites that steal your information.

flags.title: Poor Grammar and Spelling
flags.description: Official communication from SASSA is professional. Scam messages often contain spelling and grammar mistakes.

flags.title: Unusual Contact Methods
flags.description: Be wary of unexpected calls or messages from unofficial channels. Always verify the source.

checklist.title: Scam Prevention Checklist
checklist.intro: Use this checklist to make sure you are doing everything you can to stay safe from scams.

items.text: I never share my SASSA card PIN with anyone.
I only use the official SASSA website (sassa.gov.za) for information.
I ignore SMS messages that ask for money or personal details.
I have saved the official SASSA contact numbers.
I know how to report a scam.
